text:
maria: Quick Q — running into 401s when testing curl on a Windows dev box. We store the API key in REDWOOD_API_KEY and the SDKs here expect Basic auth. On mac/linux my curl header works, on Windows it fails. Any common env/encoding pitfalls?

devon: Usually it's quotes or a trailing CRLF in the env var. Windows GUIs and some setx/PowerShell flows sneak in extra characters. Also check whether the service expects base64(api_key + ':') vs base64(':' + api_key).

sam: Quick checklist: 1) make sure no surrounding quotes in the env value 2) trim whitespace/newlines 3) confirm basic encoding. Example I use in node: 
```
// node snippet
const key = (process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || '').trim();
const basic = Buffer.from(`${key}:`).toString('base64');
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Basic ${basic}` } });
```
That assumes API key is username and empty password (username:password -> key:).

jessica: Python equivalent: 
```
import os, base64
k = os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY', '').strip()
hdr = 'Basic ' + base64.b64encode(f"{k}:".encode()).decode()
# requests.get(url, headers={"Authorization": hdr})
```
Works fine if env var has no CRLF.

maria: @devon how would you confirm the exact bytes being sent? Want to rule out base64 order issue vs CRLF.

devon: Use curl verbose + echo the header: 
```
# bash/linux
auth=$(printf "%s:" "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | base64)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Basic $auth" ...
```
On PowerShell you can do:
```
$auth = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY:`"))
# but watch for inadvertent `" characters from quoting
```
But simplest: log base64 on the client and compare with a working mac build. If they differ, it's the env contents.

sam: Another Windows pitfall: using setx will persist without quotes but if you used quotes when calling setx they become part of the value. Example wrong: `setx REDWOOD_API_KEY "abc123"` -> value includes quotes. Use `setx REDWOOD_API_KEY abc123`.

jessica: Also pbcopy/clip differences. On mac folks do `echo -n $KEY | pbcopy` (no newline). On Windows `| clip` tends to include CRLF if you use echo without -n. So when pasting into an env UI or file you might pick up \r. Trim in code: `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY?.trim()` is cheap and helps.

maria: Good tips. Any Go example for folks on backend?

devon: Go: 
```
import (
  "encoding/base64"
  "os"
  "strings"
)
key := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
b := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(key + ":"))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+b)
```

sam: If you still see 401 after trimming, double-check which format the server expects. Some older clients used Basic with empty username and API key as password: `base64(":" + key)`. If you control the server or it's documented test both quickly by swapping order.

ci-bot: deploy-check: test-suite/api-auth-basic passed on linux runners, failed on windows-runner-03 (401). Investigating env encoding on runner.

jessica: For CI on Windows runners we ended up normalizing in the test harness: `os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"] = os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"].strip()` before making requests. That removed flakiness.

maria: Thanks all — going to trim in the client and re-run. If that fails I'll dump the base64 and post back. :thumbsup:

devon: If you paste the base64 here I'll sanity-check it (no secrets in chat though — redact to first/last 3 chars), e.g. `abc...xyz`

maria: Will do. Thanks!
